title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (III): Hanging the 60-Micron Vessel — Epineurial Arterioles & Why Nerves Starve Before They Die (1980–2006)

teenKit.tldr: For decades, doctors thought high blood sugar directly poisoned nerves to cause diabetes damage, but science proved the nerves actually starve first because their microscopic plumbing fails.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding that blood vessel breakdown causes nerve death rather than the reverse completely rewrites how we treat metabolic diseases like diabetes and prevent devastating amputations.
keyTakeaways: Medical dogma for years assumed that sick nerves caused the body to send them less blood, getting the timeline completely backwards.
Researchers had to master pressurized videomicroscopy to look at tiny epineurial arterioles—blood vessels thinner than a human eyelash.
Microvascular endothelial dysfunction (the blood vessel lining breaking down) is the true hidden trigger that precedes nerve failure.

vocab.meaning: A type of nerve damage associated with diabetes that causes numbness, tingling, or pain, traditionally blamed directly on sugar toxicity.
Microscopic blood vessels supplying oxygen and nutrients directly to the nerves, operating at a scale 60 to 100 microns wide.
When the delicate inner lining of blood vessels loses its ability to properly relax, dilate, and regulate blood flow.
A physical law stating that even a tiny decrease in a blood vessel's radius causes a massive, catastrophic drop in fluid flow.

quiz.question: What was the long-held medical belief about why nerves fail in diabetic patients?
options: High blood sugar directly poisoned and degraded the nerve cells over time
The immune system accidentally attacked the myelin sheath of motor neurons
Vitamin deficiencies caused the brain to stop sending signals to the limbs
Physical pressure from muscles crushed the blood vessels supplying the feet
quiz.explanation: Doctors used to view high blood glucose as a slow-acting poison that directly attacked nerves, making the nerves ask for less blood.

quiz.question: According to Dr. Mark Yorek's decades of research, what actually happens first?
options: The nerve cells die, which causes the blood vessels to shrink
Microscopic blood vessel dysfunction starves the nerve before the nerve itself fails
The brain shuts off nerve impulses to preserve core body temperature
High cholesterol physically blocks the spinal cord from transmitting signals
quiz.explanation: The research proved that microvascular plumbing fails first, starving the nerve of blood before the nerve actually starts to break down.

quiz.question: How small are the specific blood vessels (epineurial arterioles) that researchers had to study?
options: About the size of a standard drinking straw
Roughly as thick as a human finger
Thinner than a human eyelash, measuring 60 to 100 microns
Microscopic organisms invisible even to high-powered laboratory lasers
quiz.explanation: Scientists used cutting-edge pressurized videomicroscopy to zoom into vessels just 60 to 100 microns wide, which is thinner than a human eyelash.
